requests.rationale:
Hypothesis: Thermal excursion at high current limits fast charging; the 1.5C discharge from full (preceded by 0.3C CC charge to 4.2 V, CV hold, and 2 h rest, so start SOC ~1.0 per the documented procedure) provides the strongest thermal signal to identify cooling/thermal mass.

Segment 51 of record 2 is listed in the state as a constant-current 7.49996 A (1.5/h) discharge, V 3.9437->2.4999 falling, T 26.832->54.744 (+27.911 K), after a rest ending 4.1857 V following a full charge - supporting mode=1 (discharge) and start_soc=1.0. This is the largest thermal signal in cell02, best for a first thermal fit, while cell03 remains held out.

Hypothesis: Thermal excursion at high current limits fast charging (constraints: max_temperature ≤45 °C expected to bind before, or alongside, min_anode_potential ≥25 mV). The 1.5C discharge gives the largest surface-temperature signal (+25.9 K in record 3 segment 52) and is therefore the most discriminating held-out check of the cooling/thermal-mass fit.

Result rq_a5c7726c61e24bb8d61b (test 1) matched all predictions: temperature_rise 27.9114 K vs predicted 27.91, duration 39.381 min, current 7.49996 A. Record 3 segment 52 is listed in the state as a constant-current 7.49996 A (1.5/h) discharge, V 3.9577->2.5 falling, T 26.355->52.264 (+25.909 K), after segment 51 rest ending 4.1855 V following a full charge — the same documented procedure (0.3C CC charge to 4.2 V, CV hold to 50 mA, 2 h rest) as test 1, supporting mode=1 (discharge) and start_soc=1.0 as an assumption citing that procedure. This is cell03, distinct from test 1's cell02, so it is a genuine held-out check.

requests.rationale:
Hypothesis: Thermal excursion, governed primarily by fixture cooling h differing from the nominal h=10 W/m2/K, limits fast charging; a cooling-only fit to the large 1.5C temperature rise will identify h for the records' fixture, while thermal mass remains at nominal.

Test 1 (rq_a5c7726c61e24bb8d61b, record 2 segment 51, 1.5C discharge from SOC 1.0) gives the strongest cooling signal: temperature_rise 27.9114 K over 39.381 min, all predictions inside. Test 2 (rq_948f07dd1025f23efe1b, cell03) is deliberately excluded from fit_on so the resulting model version can be checked on a different cell it did not fit. Family 1 is tried first because it is the more identifiable model from a single constant-current segment without an included rest; if fit_adequate is no or the held-out check fails, family 2 or a mechanism-exposing test will follow.

requests.rationale:
Hypothesis: Thermal excursion limits fast charging — max_temperature <= 45 degC is expected to bind first, because test 1 rose 27.9114 K at 1.5C — and the family-1 failure is a thermal-mass/timescale mismatch rather than cooling alone: family 1 (rq_0480b6970eddbe8a13de) gave h=7.422 W/m2/K, RMSE 1.6681 K, bias -0.7569 K and lag-1 autocorrelation 0.994 with fit_adequate=no, so no cooling-only member explains test 1 within the noise.

Compare with prediction first: family 1's result was inside all four predicted intervals (h 7.422 vs 9.0 [4,18], RMSE 1.6681 vs 1.5 [0.1,5.0], members 3 vs 5 [1,20], k 1.0 fixed), yet fit_adequate=no with strongly structured residuals (lag-1 0.994, bias -0.7569 K, max_abs 2.9779 K) and nominal h=10 outside the 95% region [6.347,8.68]. That pattern says cooling alone gets the magnitude roughly right but misses the shape/timescale, which is exactly what adding thermal-mass scale k (family 2) can change. Fitting only test 1 (bitmask 1) preserves test 2 (rq_948f07dd1025f23efe1b, cell03, 1.5C, rise 25.9088 K) as a genuine held-out check on a different cell. Note family 2 from a constant-current segment without a rest can fix combinations of h and k only weakly — a rest trace would fix only their ratio — so adequacy and the held-out check, not the point estimates alone, will decide standing.

Hypothesis: Thermal excursion limits fast charging — max_temperature <= 45 degC is expected to bind first, since test 1 rose 27.9114 K at 1.5C from 26.8322 degC — and the thermal-mass mismatch identified in family 1 is a genuine fixture/cell thermal property, not an artefact of cell02 alone, so family 2 (h=5.224 W/m2/K, k=1.485) fitted to test 1 will also explain the held-out 1.5C discharge of cell03 (test 2, rise 25.9088 K) within the noise.

Compare with the previous prediction first: family 2 (rq_211b14645d6d3efe1a69) returned fit_adequate=yes, h=5.224 W/m2/K and k=1.485 both inside the predicted intervals, members 5 as predicted, but thermal_fit_rmse 0.1916 K fell OUTSIDE (below) the predicted interval 0.3-3.0 K centred on 1.2 K — the fit is much better than I forecast, with bias -0.0283 K and max_abs 0.4834 K versus family 1's RMSE 1.6681 K, bias -0.7569 K and lag-1 autocorrelation 0.994 (rq_0480b6970eddbe8a13de, fit_adequate=no). I now believe the limiting thermal mechanism includes an effective thermal mass ~1.485x nominal alongside weaker cooling (h 95% region [4.944,5.472] W/m2/K, nominal h=10 well outside), rather than cooling alone. That revision makes the held-out check decisive: version 2 was fitted only to test 1 (cell02, 1.5C, record 2 segment 51; res_0c41d57be7228e72831d31fc), while test 2 (rq_948f07dd1025f23efe1b, cell03, 1.5C discharge from SOC 1.0, temperature_rise 25.9088 K, duration 39.455 min, all predictions inside) is a different cell it did not fit. Per the campaign rules a design may be recommended only from a version with an adequate fit AND a passing check on tests it did not fit, so this check — not another fit on both tests — is the experiment whose result most changes the next decision. Caution: surface-temperature agreement does not validate anode potential; min_anode_potential >= 25 mV remains a model forecast, and charge above 0.3C is unvalidated by the records.

requests.rationale:
Hypothesis: Thermal excursion limits the fast charge: at the objective ambient of 25 degC, max_temperature <= 45 degC is expected to bind first (test 1 rose 27.9114 K at 1.5C, reaching ~54.7 degC in the records' fixture), with min_anode_potential >= 25 mV also potentially binding at high C-rate but remaining an unmeasured forecast. The version-2 failure is cell-to-cell / joint-parameter variation: a family-2 (cooling h + thermal-mass k) fit pooled over both cells will find a compromise h,k that explains both 1.5C discharges within noise, rather than cell02 alone.

Compare with the sealed prediction first: check_model rq_894394a191a1592180af on held-out test 2 fell OUTSIDE all intervals — heldout_coverage 0.0859 vs 0.95 [0.8,1.0], heldout_rmse 1.8185 K vs 0.4 [0.1,1.0] K, heldout_max_error 2.6849 K vs 1.0 [0.2,2.5] K, bias -1.6544 K. I now believe version 2 (rq_211b14645d6d3efe1a69: h=5.224 W/m2/K, k=1.485, fit RMSE 0.1916 K, fit_adequate=yes on test 1 only) overfits cell02 and does not transfer to cell03 (test 2, rq_948f07dd1025f23efe1b: 1.5C discharge, rise 25.9088 K vs test 1's 27.9114 K at the same current and similar duration). Therefore version 2 has no standing for a design recommendation. Pooling tests 1+2 (fit_on=3) under family 2 tests whether any single h,k in the offered family explains both cells; if fit_adequate=no, no member of family 2 explains the records and its region is not an uncertainty. If adequate, the pooled version must still pass check_model on a newly created held-out record test at a different C-rate (e.g. the 1C or C/2 discharges in the same records) before it can support optimize_protocol. Family 1 is not retried pooled first because it already failed on test 1 alone (rq_0480b6970eddbe8a13de: RMSE 1.6681 K, bias -0.7569 K, lag-1 0.994, fit_adequate=no).

requests.rationale:
Hypothesis: Thermal excursion limits the fast charge — at the objective ambient of 25 degC, max_temperature <= 45 degC is expected to bind first because test 1 rose 27.9114 K at 1.5C, with min_anode_potential >= 25 mV remaining an unmeasured forecast — and the pooled failure is cell-to-cell variation in effective h,k, not a failure of family 2 for each cell individually: family 2 fitted to test 2 alone (cell03) will be adequate but with h,k distinct from cell02's version 2.

Compare with the sealed prediction first: pooled family-2 fit rq_b506f45d4fb6dcffbd7a was inside all predicted intervals (h 5.679 vs 5.6 [4.5,7.0], k 1.567 vs 1.35 [1.0,1.6], RMSE 0.9257 vs 0.8 [0.2,1.8], members 5 as predicted) yet fit_adequate=no, with opposite residual biases (+0.7848 K on test 1, -0.8385 K on test 2) and lag-1 autocorrelations 0.956/0.971. Therefore no single family-2 member explains both records, and its 95% region [h 2.136-7.766, k 1.233-2.067] is not a usable uncertainty region. I now believe either (a) each cell is individually family-2-adequate with different h,k — cell-to-cell variation — or (b) family 2 is inadequate even per cell and a mechanism outside the family is present. Version 2 fitted to cell02 alone was adequate (rq_211b14645d6d3efe1a69: h=5.224, k=1.485, RMSE 0.1916 K) but failed its held-out check on cell03 (rq_894394a191a1592180af: coverage 0.0859, RMSE 1.8185 K, bias -1.6544 K, forecast max 53.958 degC vs observed 51.638 degC), consistent with cell03 running cooler at the same 1.5C (rise 25.9088 K in test 2, rq_948f07dd1025f23efe1b, vs 27.9114 K in test 1, rq_a5c7726c61e24bb8d61b). Fitting family 2 to test 2 alone is the most decision-changing next step: adequacy plus a region distinct from version 2's [h 4.944-5.472, k 1.45-1.525] would establish cell-to-cell variation and rule out any pooled record model for design, pushing learning toward lab-fixture tests; inadequacy would establish that no offered family explains even a single cell03 record.

Hypothesis: Thermal excursion limits the fast charge in the lab fixture: max_temperature <= 45 degC is expected to bind first, because the 1.5C record discharges rose 25.9088-27.9114 K, while min_anode_potential >= 25 mV remains an unmeasured model forecast. The record fits do not transfer: version 2 (cell02) failed its held-out check on cell03, the pooled family-2 fit was inadequate, and the cell03-only fit is adequate with a distinct region, so the lab fixture's h and k must be measured in the lab itself.

Compare with the sealed prediction first: the cell03-only family-2 fit (rq_b5d99c8a7d08382f247d) was inside all predicted intervals (h 6.161 vs 6.8 [4.5,9.5] W/m2/K, k 1.655 vs 1.35 [0.9,1.8], RMSE 0.1525 vs 0.35 [0.05,1.2] K, members 4 vs 5 [1,10]) and fit_adequate=yes. Its 95% region h [5.896,6.399], k [1.62,1.695] does not overlap version 2's region for cell02 (rq_211b14645d6d3efe1a69: h [4.944,5.472], k [1.45,1.525]), confirming cell-to-cell variation as the explanation for the pooled fit's inadequacy (rq_b506f45d4fb6dcffbd7a: fit_adequate=no, opposite biases +0.7848/-0.8385 K) and for version 2's failed held-out check (rq_894394a191a1592180af: coverage 0.0859, RMSE 1.8185 K). Therefore no record-based version has standing for a design in the lab's fixture, which the objective statement says may differ from the records' fixture. A 1.5C lab charge at 25 degC ambient gives the largest thermal signal (matching the 1.5C record discharges) plus a 60 min logged rest whose cooling trace constrains the thermal-mass-to-cooling ratio, making it the most discriminating first measurement of the lab fixture. This is a measurement, not a design recommendation: it may exceed 45 degC, and a lab test measures surface temperature, voltage and current only, never the anode potential.

requests.rationale:
Hypothesis: Thermal excursion limits the fast charge in the lab fixture: max_temperature <= 45 degC binds first, as the 1.5C lab charge reached 49.79 degC at 25 degC ambient, while min_anode_potential >= 25 mV remains an unmeasured forecast. A cooling + thermal-mass (family 2) model can explain the lab test's charge heating and 60 min rest cooling, with h,k for the lab fixture distinct from either record cell.

Compare with the sealed prediction first: lab test 3 (rq_da111fd8258b0ee8490d, res_dbe14a29e80473ab102f43e3) gave charge_time_80 28.29 min, OUTSIDE the predicted 28.0 [27.9,28.1] min (just above the solver-bound interval), max_temperature 49.79 degC inside 46.0 [38,54] degC, temperature_end 28.09 degC inside, and noise_temperature 0.15 delta_degC as predicted. The time miss is small (0.29 min vs ±0.05 min solver tolerance stated for charge_time_80) and does not change the decision; the temperature result does: 49.79 ±0.1 degC exceeds the 45 degC constraint, so this 1.5C protocol is infeasible in the lab fixture and max_temperature is the constraint expected to bind.

The records cannot supply the lab fixture's parameters: cell02 family-2 version 2 (rq_211b14645d6d3efe1a69: h=5.224, k=1.485, adequate) failed its held-out check on cell03 (rq_894394a191a1592180af), the pooled fit was inadequate (rq_b506f45d4fb6dcffbd7a), and cell03-only version 4 (rq_b5d99c8a7d08382f247d: h=6.161, k=1.655, adequate) has a 95% region non-overlapping cell02's. Hence fit family 2 — which was adequate per-cell in the records, whereas family 1 was inadequate even on test 1 — to lab test 3 alone (fit_on=4). Test 3 includes a 60 min logged rest, whose cooling trace constrains the thermal-mass-to-cooling ratio (it cannot fix h and k separately alone), together with the strong 24.79 K rise during charge. No other lab test exists yet to hold out, so after this fit a second, different lab protocol must be created for check_model before any design recommendation.

Hypothesis: Thermal excursion limits fast charging in the lab fixture: max_temperature <= 45 degC is expected to bind before the anode forecast, because the 1.5C lab charge reached 49.79 degC at 25 degC ambient. A 1.0C charge should remain below 45 degC while still producing a substantial thermal signal that discriminates version 5's h=5.744 W/m2/K, k=1.245 from alternatives.

Compare with the sealed prediction first: fit rq_7380df95c3e00baa135a to lab test 3 was inside all predicted intervals (h 5.744 vs 6.0 [4.5,7.5] W/m2/K, k 1.245 vs 1.5 [1.0,2.0], RMSE 0.1461 vs 0.3 [0.05,1.0] K, members 5 as predicted) and fit_adequate=yes, with bias 0.0102 K and rest RMSE 0.1404 K. That gives version 5 an adequate fit, but per campaign rules it cannot support a design until checked on a test it did not fit. The only lab test, test 3 (rq_da111fd8258b0ee8490d, 1.5C, max_temperature 49.79 degC, infeasible vs 45 degC), was its fit source. A 1.0C charge at the same 25 degC ambient and 60 min rest differs in C-rate (within version 5's validity c_rate [1.5,1.5] it is an extrapolation in rate, so the check is informative rather than guaranteed), exercises heating plus rest cooling, and its deterministic charge time is 42.0 min for 10-80% SOC. This lab test measures surface temperature, voltage and current only; min_anode_potential >= 25 mV remains a model forecast and is not measured here.

Hypothesis: Thermal excursion limits the fast charge in the lab fixture: max_temperature <= 45 degC is expected to bind first, because the 1.5C lab charge reached 49.79 degC at 25 degC ambient while the 1.0C lab charge reached only 41.42 degC; min_anode_potential >= 25 mV remains an unmeasured model forecast. Family 2 fitted to lab test 3 (version 5, h=5.744 W/m2/K, k=1.245) captures the lab fixture's cooling and thermal mass, so it will also explain the held-out 1.0C lab test 4 within the noise.

Compare with the sealed prediction first: lab test 4 (rq_7b21054f95068786ac00, res_890f62aa9be5b2f13d44a987) was inside all predicted intervals — charge_time_80 42.0 min vs 42.0 [41.4,42.6] min, max_temperature 41.42 degC vs 38.0 [32,44] degC, temperature_end 27.29 degC vs 27.0 [25.5,29] degC, noise_temperature 0.15 delta_degC as predicted. Its max_temperature 41.42 ± 0.1 degC passes the 45 degC constraint, unlike test 3 at 1.5C (rq_da111fd8258b0ee8490d: 49.79 degC, infeasible), confirming temperature is the constraint expected to bind as C-rate rises; no lab test measures min_anode_potential, so that constraint remains a forecast. Version 5 (rq_7380df95c3e00baa135a) was fitted only to test 3, with fit_adequate=yes, RMSE 0.1461 K, bias 0.0102 K and a tight 95% region h [5.723,5.758] W/m2/K, k [1.24,1.25]. Test 4 is a different protocol (1.0C in all four steps, 25 degC ambient, 60 min rest) that version 5 did not fit, so this check is outside its stated validity c_rate [1.5,1.5] and is an informative extrapolation test rather than a guaranteed pass. Per campaign rules a design may be recommended only from a version with an adequate fit AND a passing check_model on tests it did not fit, with no check failing it; this check is therefore the experiment whose result most changes the next decision — pass leads to optimize_protocol under version 5, failure leads to refitting/lab learning and no design.

Hypothesis: Thermal excursion limits the fast charge in the lab fixture: max_temperature <= 45 degC is expected to bind first, because the uniform 1.5C lab charge reached 49.79 degC at 25 degC ambient while the uniform 1.0C charge reached only 41.42 degC; min_anode_potential >= 25 mV is the second, forecast-only constraint and may bind at high SOC in the design search. Model version 5 (cooling + thermal mass fitted to lab test 3) captures the lab fixture well enough that the fastest member-feasible design lies between the 1.0C and 1.5C uniform protocols.

Compare with the sealed prediction first: check_model rq_54760f6aa55d4bf6562f of version 5 on held-out lab test 4 was inside all predicted intervals — heldout_coverage 0.9625 vs 0.95 [0.8,1.0], heldout_rmse 0.1533 K vs 0.3 [0.1,1.0] K, heldout_max_error 0.49 K vs 0.8 [0.2,2.5] K, bias 0.0092 K, forecast max 41.05 degC vs observed 41.42 degC. I now believe version 5 generalises across C-rate in the lab fixture (1.5C fit test 3 to 1.0C held-out test 4), so it meets the standing required for a design search: fit_adequate=yes on test 3 (rq_7380df95c3e00baa135a: h=5.744 W/m2/K, k=1.245, RMSE 0.1461 K) plus this passing held-out check, with no check failing it. The constraint expected to bind is max_temperature <= 45 degC: test 3 at 1.5C measured 49.79 ±0.1 degC (infeasible) and test 4 at 1.0C measured 41.42 ±0.1 degC (feasible), bracketing the feasible rate; min_anode_potential >= 25 mV is never measured by a lab test and remains a version-5 forecast, which the search must satisfy for every member. Ambient 25 degC is the objective setpoint and matches both lab tests. This is the experiment whose result most changes the next decision: it either yields a concrete candidate protocol to lab-test or shows no member-feasible design exists under the only model version with standing.

conclusion.text:
Recommendation rests on the optimize_protocol result rq_c7c2d9d06f43ad1fe752 under model version 5: a four-step charge at 25 degC ambient of 1.5C (10-27.5% SOC), 1.5C (27.5-45%), 1.2C (45-62.5%), 0.8C (62.5-80%), with charge_time_80 35.875 +- 0.05 min, max_temperature 44.745 +- 0.1 degC (limit <=45 degC) and min_anode_potential 27.462 +- 0.5 mV (limit >=25 mV) for the worst member; all five members meet both limits (member max_temperature 44.685-44.745 degC, min_anode_potential 27.462-27.582 mV). This is a candidate that meets the constraints in simulation; it is not proven to be the fastest possible, and speed is not compared because there is no computational baseline that meets the constraints and this objective runs no reference search (assessment / rq_c7c2d9d06f43ad1fe752 comparison cmp_c16c98525310040aece76208: verdict inconclusive, speed not compared).

Model standing: version 5 is family 2 (cooling + thermal mass) fitted only to lab test 3 (rq_7380df95c3e00baa135a: h=5.744 W/m2/K, k=1.245, 95% region h [5.723,5.758], k [1.24,1.25], RMSE 0.1461 K, fit_adequate=yes), and it passed a held-out check on lab test 4, which it did not fit (rq_54760f6aa55d4bf6562f: heldout_coverage 0.9625, heldout_rmse 0.1533 K, heldout_max_error 0.49 K, forecast max 41.05 degC vs observed 41.42 degC); the design result itself reports model_standing supported=true. The record-based versions could not be used for design: pooled records were fit-inadequate and per-cell regions did not overlap (rq_b506f45d4fb6dcffbd7a, rq_211b14645d6d3efe1a69, rq_b5d99c8a7d08382f247d), so learning was moved to the lab fixture.

Constraint expected to bind, and observed: max_temperature. Uniform lab charges bracketed it at 25 degC ambient — 1.5C reached 49.79 +- 0.1 degC (rq_da111fd8258b0ee8490d, infeasible) and 1.0C reached 41.42 +- 0.1 degC (rq_7b21054f95068786ac00, feasible) — and the recommended design's worst-member temperature is only 0.255 degC below the 45 degC limit.

The recommended protocol itself has not been run as a lab test: the lab-test budget is spent (2 of 2, tests 3 and 4), and a lab test would in any case measure only surface temperature, voltage and current — the anode/plating margin remains a version-5 forecast, never a measurement, and is unvalidated by the supplied records (no charge faster than 0.3C and no plating measurement in them).
unresolved_reasons: The recommended design (rq_c7c2d9d06f43ad1fe752) has not been verified by a lab_charge of its exact 1.5/1.5/1.2/0.8C protocol: the lab-test budget is spent (2 of 2). Its 0.255 degC temperature margin is small relative to the 0.37 degC forecast-observed difference seen on held-out lab test 4 (rq_54760f6aa55d4bf6562f), so lab confirmation would be the next experiment if budget allowed.

min_anode_potential >= 25 mV is a model forecast only: no lab test measures anode potential, and the supplied Chen 2020 records contain no plating measurement and no charge above 0.3C, so the plating margin (forecast 27.462 mV) cannot be validated from this evidence.

Speed is not compared: there is no computational baseline meeting the constraints and no reference search for this objective, so the 35.875 min candidate meets the constraints in simulation but cannot be claimed faster than a reference or the fastest possible.

No thermocouple calibration is on file for the records, and exact thermocouple placement beyond 'taped to the cell surface' is not established; surface-temperature accuracy rests on the stated noise treatment used in the fits.

investigation.documentation:
LG M50 cells (LG INR21700 M50, nominal capacity 5.0 Ah), one file per cell, exported from a Maccor cycler; the cells sat in a thermal chamber. Published validation tests: Chen et al. 2020, "Development of Experimental Techniques for Parameterization of Multi-scale Lithium-ion Battery Models", J. Electrochem. Soc. 167, 080534; data on Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.4032561 (CC BY 4.0).
Procedure on every cell: a C/10 discharge; after each discharge a 0.3C constant-current charge to 4.2 V with a constant-voltage hold to 50 mA; discharges from full to 2.5 V at C/2, 1C and 1.5C; 2 h rests between steps.
Instruments: a thermocouple taped to the cell surface, and a second sensor in the chamber air. The current is logged as a magnitude; the mode column says C (charge), D (discharge) or R (rest). The files hold no faster charge and no plating measurement. No thermocouple calibration is on file.
